stories.title: Nvidia releases open Nemotron 3.5 Super VL and compact Bolt models for agents
stories.summary: Nvidia has released Nemotron 3.5 Super VL, an open 120-billion-parameter multimodal model for enterprise AI agents, alongside two smaller Bolt models, including a 74B-A9B variant quantized to run on 24GB of memory.
stories.more: Super VL is aimed at enterprise agentic workloads and is openly released with 120 billion parameters. Nvidia says dozens of organizations are already fine-tuning it, though getting the most performance reportedly still depends on using Nvidia's own hardware. Alongside it, Nvidia released two smaller Bolt models meant to let agents run on local machines rather than in the cloud. One of these, the Nemotron 3.5 Bolt 74B-A9B vision-language model, uses native 2-bit quantization to fit within 24GB of memory, with GGUF-format builds shared on Hugging Face for local use. The excerpts do not give benchmark comparisons against other open models or specify a license.

stories.title: Google positions Gemini 4 Argon as a single AI model for robot control
stories.summary: Google's Gemini 4 Argon controls robots, generates simulations from photos or sketches, and evaluates training videos, scoring 87% on Google's own ERQA benchmark, though demo prompts still show heavy reliance on human guidance.
stories.more: Gemini 4 Argon is pitched as a single model that can handle multiple robotics-related tasks: direct robot control, generating simulations from photos or sketches, and evaluating training videos. On Google's own ERQA benchmark, it scores 87 percent. However, the published example prompts reportedly still require substantial human guidance to get useful results, suggesting a gap between the benchmark score and real-world autonomy. Because the benchmark is Google's own, independent verification of the 87 percent figure is not available from this excerpt. It is also unclear how this model compares to competitors' robotics-focused models.

stories.title: OpenAI's GPT-6-Astra solves 49 of 50 unpublished physics research problems
stories.summary: On the TheoPhysEval benchmark, GPT-6-Astra solved 49 of 50 unpublished theoretical physics calculations as accurately as leading specialists, at roughly $2.40 per problem, though researchers say the model still lacks research 'taste.'
stories.more: The benchmark, TheoPhysEval, tests unpublished theoretical physics calculations rather than problems the model could have seen in training. In some cases where the agent appeared to fail, the experts' own reference solutions reportedly turned out to be wrong instead. Researchers quoted say physics has not yet had a breakthrough comparable to recent progress in mathematics, attributing this to the model lacking 'taste' in choosing promising directions. Despite that, they say autonomous, top-level AI research in physics could still arrive soon. The excerpt cuts off while describing consequences for young physicists, so what those consequences are is not fully clear from the text.

stories.title: Mistral releases Timestral, compact zero-shot probabilistic forecasting models
stories.summary: Mistral launched Timestral, a family of four CPU-efficient probabilistic forecasting models ranging from 5M to 209M parameters, designed to work zero-shot without task-specific training.
stories.more: Timestral targets probabilistic forecasting, meaning it predicts a range of likely outcomes rather than a single point estimate. It ships in four sizes, from 5M to 209M parameters, letting users trade off size for accuracy. The models are described as CPU-efficient, suggesting they are meant to run without requiring GPU infrastructure. They are also zero-shot ready, meaning they can be applied to new forecasting tasks without additional fine-tuning. The excerpt does not specify what benchmarks back the 'state-of-the-art' claim or give release details like licensing.

stories.title: Apertus team extends open Apertus models to multimodal reasoning with Apertus 1.5
stories.summary: Apertus 1.5 continues pretraining the open Apertus 1.0 models on trillions of additional tokens, adding image and audio understanding and a 262,144-token context window, aiming to show open infrastructure can rival closed providers at scale.
stories.more: The Apertus family is built entirely in the open, trained on documented data, as an alternative to depending on a handful of providers. Apertus 1.5 continues pretraining the 8B and 70B Apertus 1.0 models, adding 4T and 2T tokens respectively. The update adds image and audio understanding on top of the original text-only models. It also extends the context window fourfold, to 262,144 tokens. The excerpt does not specify benchmark results or a release date for weights.

stories.title: Researchers unlock faster asynchronous RL rollouts with INT4 KV cache quantization
stories.summary: A new paper finds that quantizing the KV cache to INT4 speeds up asynchronous rollouts in reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards more than weight-only or weight-activation quantization, as rising concurrency concentrates KV workload per decode step.
stories.more: Asynchronous rollout is used in RLVR training to cut idle time during long-tail generation, but sustained concurrency concentrates context processing into fewer decode steps. The researchers characterize this increased 'KV concentration' and its effect on serving cost. In matched-workload comparisons, INT4 KV cache quantization gives substantially bigger speedups than quantizing weights alone or weights and activations together. The excerpt is cut off before giving concrete speedup numbers or full method details, so those specifics remain unclear from the available text.

stories.title: New 'Hybrid Reasoning Agents' architecture blends latent and text-based reasoning
stories.summary: A paper proposes Hybrid Reasoning Agents, which dynamically switch between efficient internal 'latent' reasoning and transparent text-based reasoning, aiming to give LLM agents both speed and the tool access text interaction provides.
stories.more: Today's LLM agents reason and act almost entirely through text, which keeps their reasoning transparent and tool use straightforward but can be inefficient. Latent reasoning offers a faster internal medium, but on its own it lacks native tool access and makes an agent's reasoning hard to inspect. HybridAgents are designed to navigate between the two modes throughout a single, unified generation process rather than picking one approach upfront. The excerpt describes the motivation and high-level architecture but is cut off before detailing results or benchmarks, so the efficiency or capability gain is not yet clear from the text.

items.title: Hybrid Reasoning Agents
items.excerpt: How can we build an agent that thinks beyond human language, yet still acts through it in the external environment? Modern LLM agents still reason and interact through text, while latent reasoning offers an efficient internal medium but lacks native tool access and reasoning transparency. We bridge these two directions with Hybrid Reasoning Agents (HybridAgents), which dynamically navigate between latent reasoning and text-based interaction throughout a unified generation process.
